title: Agentforce Sales Consultant Certification - Practice Exam
description: 60-question timed practice exam mirroring the official Summer '25 Agentforce Sales Consultant blueprint domain weights. 105 minutes, pass with 73% or higher.

questions.question: Partners need to register deals and see only their own opportunities in a branded site. What do you recommend?
options: A scheduled report subscription
Quip document sharing on each opportunity
Territory assignment rules on the account
An Experience Cloud partner site with sharing rules
questions.explanation: A branded external portal for partners is an Experience Cloud partner site, since a report, a Quip document, or a territory rule never provides an external login surface.

questions.question: A team logs email manually today and now wants every Outlook message and meeting logged to Salesforce with tracking, without a fixed step sequence. Which do you choose?
options: Salesforce Inbox
Sales Engagement cadences
Enterprise Territory Management
Opportunity Forecasting
questions.explanation: Salesforce Inbox augments the rep's own mailbox and calendar with logging and tracking without imposing a cadence, which is what the requirement describes.

questions.question: A VP asks for a feature that predicts which open opportunities are most likely to close so reps can prioritize their day. Which layer is the correct choice?
options: An Agentforce agent topic built in Agent Builder
A Salesforce Meetings insight
Einstein Opportunity Scoring
Enterprise Territory Management assignment rules
questions.explanation: The verb is predict, and Einstein Opportunity Scoring ranks opportunities from a trained model, whereas an agent reasons and acts rather than scoring.

questions.question: A firm wants an agent to draft and send follow-up emails autonomously, but legal requires that no discounting language ever reaches a customer. Which is the strongest design?
options: Constrain the topic instructions and route discount-related replies to a human approval action
Give the agent a longer instruction and rely on the model to comply
Disable the Einstein Trust Layer so the agent has fewer restrictions
Turn off data masking so the agent can see more fields
questions.explanation: Narrow topic instructions plus an approval action for the risky path is the bounded design, and disabling the Trust Layer or masking would weaken protections rather than solve the legal requirement.

questions.question: A rep has qualified a deal and wants to send a formal quote. What must be in place on the Opportunity?
options: A scheduled report subscription on the opportunity
Einstein Activity Capture enabled for the rep
An active territory model that includes the account
Products added from a price book so a Quote can be generated and synced
questions.explanation: Quoting starts from the opportunity's products on a price book, and the generated Quote syncs its lines back to the opportunity, so the other options do not enable quoting.

questions.question: A team requires reps to follow a repeatable multi-touch sequence of calls, emails, and tasks, with a prioritised call list each morning. Which feature fits?
options: Opportunity Forecasting
Sales Engagement cadences
Enterprise Territory Management
Salesforce Inbox
questions.explanation: Sales Engagement cadences drive the sequenced multi-touch steps and the Work Queue prioritises who to contact, while forecasting only rolls up commit numbers.

questions.question: You need one report that compares open pipeline and closed-won blocks built from different report types. Which report format do you use?
options: Tabular
Summary
Matrix
Joined
questions.explanation: A joined report combines blocks from different report types into one layout, which Tabular and the grouped formats cannot do.

questions.question: Managers need a weekly roll-up of each rep's Commit and Best Case amounts against quota. Which feature delivers that?
options: Opportunity Forecasting
Einstein Opportunity Scoring
Salesforce Inbox
Sales Engagement
questions.explanation: Opportunity Forecasting rolls forecast categories up against quota, whereas scoring returns a propensity and the other two drive activity or mailbox logging.

questions.question: An admin wants forecast numbers to reflect a newly carved set of territories. Which setup is required first?
options: A new Einstein scoring model
A Sales Engagement cadence
A Salesforce Inbox package
Enterprise Territory Management
questions.explanation: Territory-based forecasting depends on Enterprise Territory Management, because without it forecasts roll up by role.

questions.question: A stakeholder wants to chart how pipeline coverage changed over a year, but the live report shows only current values. Which feature do you use?
options: A reporting snapshot
A cross filter
A bucket field
A joined report
questions.explanation: A reporting snapshot writes report results into a custom object over time, which is what lets you chart change the live report cannot show.

questions.question: Before going live with an Agentforce sales agent, the team must protect customer data sent to the model. Which control applies?
options: Turn off field history tracking on the objects
Enable Salesforce Meetings for the pilot group
The Einstein Trust Layer with data masking and zero data retention
Create a scheduled report subscription for the transcripts
questions.explanation: The Trust Layer sits inline between the agent and the model and provides masking and zero data retention, while none of the other options touch data sent to the LLM.

questions.question: A VP asks you to add a ranking that orders each open opportunity by likelihood to close so reps can sort their pipeline. Which capability fits?
options: Generative email drafting in Agentforce
Sales Engagement cadences
Einstein Opportunity Scoring
Salesforce Inbox
questions.explanation: Only the predictive scoring model returns a likelihood ranking, while generative features produce language rather than a number.

questions.question: On a stakeholder map, what does an unengaged high-power stakeholder represent?
options: A low priority contact who can be dropped from updates
A risk to the project who needs a targeted engagement plan
An end user who will adopt automatically once the system ships
A sponsor by virtue of their seniority alone
questions.explanation: High power and low interest is the quadrant a project must keep satisfied, so an unengaged high-power stakeholder is a risk requiring a targeted engagement plan; seniority alone does not make someone the sponsor, which is a role the client names.

questions.question: During a workshop a department head says the new system must work exactly like the old one. What have you actually captured?
options: A confirmed functional requirement you can build to
A non-functional requirement about usability
A solution preference that hides the real requirement, so you keep asking why until you reach the underlying outcome
An acceptance criterion for UAT
questions.explanation: A statement about the old system is a proposed solution, not an outcome, so the correct move is to keep asking why until the business need it protects is exposed; treating it as a functional requirement locks an old workaround into the new build.

questions.question: Why does the Agentforce agent user belong in the same access review as human employees?
options: Because agents bypass all sharing rules
Because the agent acts with the agent user's permissions, so over-privilege becomes an escalation path
Because agents cannot be assigned permission sets
Because agent access expires every 30 days
questions.explanation: The agent operates with its own identity and permissions, so an over-privileged agent user lets anyone who influences the agent influence what it can do.

questions.question: You must load 300,000 Contacts that relate to Accounts already in production, and the load may be rerun. What should you use?
options: Data Loader with an external ID upsert, after the parent Accounts exist
The Data Import Wizard, because it matches on name
An unlocked package that includes the data
A change set containing the Contact metadata
questions.explanation: Data Loader handles this volume, the external ID makes the upsert idempotent on a rerun, and loading after the parent Accounts exist satisfies the lookup order.

questions.question: UAT is finished and the client's business lead says the system looks good in the steering meeting. What makes that milestone contractually real?
options: A verbal thank-you recorded in the steering minutes
A signed acceptance document that references the acceptance criteria in the SOW
A green status report from the delivery lead
A successful cutover rehearsal
questions.explanation: Acceptance closes the phase only when it is documented and tied to the criteria the client already agreed to, so a signed acceptance document that references the SOW criteria is the gate; a green report is sentiment, not acceptance.

questions.question: A user holds a permission set that grants Modify All Data. You assign a more restrictive profile. What is the user's effective access?
options: The profile wins, because a profile is the baseline
The permission is removed, because the restrictive profile overrides it
The union applies, so the user keeps Modify All Data until the permission set is unassigned
Access depends on the user's login IP range
questions.explanation: Effective access is the union of the profile and every assigned permission set, and only a muting permission set inside a group subtracts, so the assignment must be removed.

questions.question: Your sponsor asks when success metrics for an Agentforce sales rollout should be defined. What do you advise?
options: After go-live, once real usage data exists
During user acceptance testing, once configuration is frozen
Prior to implementation, with the business, as part of the readiness assessment
Only if the project runs over budget
questions.explanation: Metrics must be set prior to implementation so there is an unbiased baseline, and they are agreed with the business rather than with the build team alone.

questions.question: Which measurement best identifies friction inside the AI agent itself?
options: The number of logins to the org
The number of records created in the month
The share of sessions escalated to a human and the topics behind them
The average page load time of the console
questions.explanation: Agent Analytics reports sessions, resolutions, and escalations, and the escalation topics point directly at the prompt, action, or data that needs work.

questions.question: A production deployment fails at the coverage gate. What is the correct fix?
options: Redeploy with NoTestRun, which is allowed for production
Deploy with the CLI ignore-errors flag
Add Apex tests that raise code coverage to at least 75 percent
Deploy during a maintenance window
questions.explanation: Production requires Apex tests to run in the target org with at least 75 percent coverage, and NoTestRun is not available for production deployments.

questions.question: A program has an executive sponsor and a detailed communication plan, yet adoption stalls in week two. Which readiness element was most likely missing?
options: A larger Developer Pro sandbox
More Apex test coverage
Additional permission sets
User champions from the most affected group involved in design
questions.explanation: An executive sponsor without user champions from the most affected group involved in design stalls once the sponsor stops repeating the message, which readiness assessment exists to catch.

questions.question: A production deployment introduced a regression two days after go-live. What is the deployment reality?
options: Use the rollback button on the Deployment Status page
Refresh the Full sandbox to revert production
Redeploy the last known good package or change set from source control
Do nothing, because metadata deployments revert automatically on failure
questions.explanation: Metadata deployments have no rollback, so the recovery path is redeploying the last known good version from source control, which is why versioned paths matter.

questions.question: Users were granted the new Agentforce app a month ago and have opened it twice. What is your first diagnostic step?
options: Send a training satisfaction survey
Verify the permission set assignment and app visibility using Login As
Refresh the Full sandbox
Add more fields to the record page
questions.explanation: Access precedes adoption, so confirming the permission set assignment and what the user actually sees with Login As separates a missing grant from a genuine usage problem.

questions.question: What does the Setup Audit Trail give you during a post-implementation review?
options: A log of setup changes covering about the last 180 days
A live stream of every user click in the org
Full transcripts of every agent session
Event-level telemetry for all users without an add-on license
questions.explanation: The Setup Audit Trail records setup changes for roughly 180 days, which is why a review that spans longer than that must export the trail before the window rolls.

questions.question: Data quality in the target objects is poor and unverified, and the client wants the highest-value use case shipped first. What do you sequence first?
options: The highest-value use case regardless of the state of the data
Whichever use case the loudest executive sponsors
A data-remediation foundation slice, because a use case is only as good as the data underneath it
Every use case at once to save elapsed time
questions.explanation: Value cannot be realized on unreliable data, so a data-remediation foundation slice comes first even though it is less visible; sequencing the high-value use case onto bad data teaches the organization to distrust the platform.

questions.question: A sales user keeps forgetting which field to update on the new record page. Which training mechanism puts the instruction where they are already looking?
options: A printed job aid left at the desk
An in-app guidance prompt on the record page
A Full Copy sandbox refresh
A change set containing the field
questions.explanation: In-app guidance renders on the page the user is viewing, which solves the last mile that classroom training and job aids lose over time.

questions.question: A managed package installed in your org is consuming your CPU governor limits. What is true?
options: Managed package Apex runs in an isolated limits context
Apex in managed packages still counts against your org's governor limits
You can edit the package's Apex to reduce its consumption
Governor limits apply only to your own Apex
questions.explanation: Packaged Apex executes inside your org against your limits, and because package components are locked you cannot edit it to reduce consumption.

questions.question: An opportunity line has a quantity of ten, a sales price of two hundred dollars, and a ten percent discount. What does Total Price equal?
options: Quantity times List Price
Quantity times Sales Price plus the discount
Quantity times Sales Price times one minus the discount
The standard price book UnitPrice for the product
questions.explanation: Total Price is Quantity times Sales Price times one minus the discount, giving one thousand eight hundred dollars here, and that figure is what rolls into the opportunity Amount.

questions.question: Can a sharing rule remove access from a group that already has it?
options: Yes, if the rule is criteria-based
Only on custom objects
No, because sharing rules only extend the access the OWD and role hierarchy provide
Yes, when the target is a public group
questions.explanation: Sharing rules are additive only, so removing access requires a change to the OWD, object permissions, or field-level security rather than a sharing rule.

questions.question: The Standard and Enterprise teams must use different stage sets on the same Opportunity object. What do you configure?
options: Two Opportunity record types, each assigned a different sales process
Two separate Opportunity Stage picklists
Two page layouts on one record type
A validation rule that hides stages per team
questions.explanation: A sales process defines which global Stage values a record type may use, so two record types each pointed at their own process is the supported pattern.

questions.question: Reps updated stages faithfully but the forecast is still wrong. What most likely explains it?
options: The opportunity amounts were never converted to the corporate currency
The reps used the wrong campaign influence model
The opportunity team members were not added
A stage is mapped to the wrong forecast category, and the forecast is driven by forecast category, not the stage name
questions.explanation: The forecast reads the forecast category a stage maps to, so a faithful stage update still misstates the forecast when the stage-to-category mapping is wrong.

questions.question: Which configuration makes contact visibility follow the account's sharing?
options: Controlled by Parent as the Contact organization-wide default
Public Read Only on Contact
A criteria-based Contact sharing rule
Grant Access Using Hierarchies cleared on Contact
questions.explanation: Setting the Contact OWD to Controlled by Parent makes contacts inherit their account's access, so no separate contact sharing model is needed.

questions.question: A validation rule references a field the running user cannot see because of field-level security. What happens on save?
options: The rule is skipped for that user
The rule evaluates normally because validation formulas ignore field-level security
The save errors out with a permissions message
The restricted field becomes visible to the user
questions.explanation: Field-level security governs visibility and edit access, not formula evaluation, so the validation rule still reads the field and evaluates normally.

questions.question: A rep converts a Lead whose record type is Enterprise. The rep's profile default Account record type is Standard. What record type does the new Account get?
options: Enterprise, inherited from the Lead
Standard, the new owner's profile default
The org default Account record type regardless of profile
None; accounts created by conversion have no record type
questions.explanation: Conversion assigns the new owner's profile default record type rather than the Lead's type, which is why orgs that need inheritance build an explicit mapping.

questions.question: You muted Read on an object in a permission set group's muting permission set. What else is muted?
options: Only Read is muted
Read and nothing else in the group
Create, Edit, Delete, View All Records, and Modify All Records
Only Modify All Records
questions.explanation: Muting cascades through permission dependencies, and because Create, Edit, Delete, View All, and Modify All are unusable without read, they are muted along with it.

questions.question: A user must collaborate on one deal while the rest of the account stays hidden. What do you configure?
options: An Opportunity Team membership for that opportunity
An Account Team membership
A change to the user's role
A change to the organization-wide default
questions.explanation: An Opportunity Team grants access to that opportunity only, which fits a deal-specific need, whereas an Account Team and an OWD change would open the whole account.

questions.question: In the save order of execution, which of these runs first?
options: Before-save record-triggered Flow
Custom validation rules
After Apex triggers
After-save record-triggered Flow
questions.explanation: Before-save Flows run before validation rules and before triggers, which is exactly why they cannot be used to evade a validation rule.

questions.question: Which feature applies a different exchange rate for different date ranges so converted opportunity amounts match the rate in effect when the deal was recorded?
options: Standard multi-currency conversion using the current active rate
Advanced Currency Management with dated exchange rates
A user's personal currency setting
The corporate currency setting alone
questions.explanation: Dated exchange rates under Advanced Currency Management bind each converted amount to the rate in effect on its date, while the standard conversion uses the current active rate and drifts retroactively.

questions.question: A rep syncs a quote to its opportunity. What happens to the opportunity products and Amount?
options: The opportunity products are copied up to the quote and the quote changes
Nothing changes until the opportunity is closed
The quote's line items are copied onto the opportunity's line items, overwriting its products, and the opportunity Amount updates from them
Only the opportunity contacts are updated from the quote
questions.explanation: Quote sync flows from the quote to the opportunity, overwriting the opportunity's line items and recomputing the Amount, so any prior manual edit to those lines is lost.

questions.question: An org has multiple currencies enabled. Which statement about a single opportunity is true?
options: One opportunity can hold products priced in several currencies at once
The corporate currency is set separately for each user
A single quote can mix currencies within its line items
A single opportunity uses exactly one currency, and every price book entry for its products must be in that same currency
questions.explanation: An opportunity transacts in exactly one currency and its price book entries must match it, so a product priced in another currency has no entry to bind to on that deal.

questions.question: A compliance officer asks two things: prove who changed an Opportunity Amount six months ago, and satisfy a new policy requiring ten years of retention. What is the correct recommendation?
options: Standard Field History Tracking covers both, because its retention is indefinite
Export the Opportunity table to a spreadsheet archive every month
Enable Field History Tracking for the six month need and Field Audit Trail for the ten year policy, noting that Field Audit Trail access is API only and needs a Shield or Field Audit Trail license
Turn on Debug Logs for all users and retain the log files
questions.explanation: Standard tracking retains only 18 to 24 months and caps at 20 fields per object, so the ten year policy requires Field Audit Trail, which archives to FieldHistoryArchive, retains until deleted, and is API only. A spreadsheet export is not an audit trail, and Debug Logs are not a field history.

questions.question: An admin must import 120,000 Contacts reliably and repeatably, and the target object supports the API. Which tool fits?
options: Data Import Wizard, because it enforces validation rules
The Data Import Wizard in several runs, since it is the safest option
Data Loader, because it handles up to 5 million records while the Data Import Wizard stops at 50,000
A manual paste into the UI list view
questions.explanation: 120,000 exceeds the Data Import Wizard's 50,000 record limit, and Data Loader's larger ceiling and object coverage make it the tool for the volume. Duplicate rules apply to both tools, so duplicate handling is not what decides the tool.

questions.question: A nightly upsert job fails halfway, and the team wants to rerun it without creating duplicate Contacts. What makes the rerun safe?
options: Deleting all the loaded records before rerunning
Running an upsert that matches on the external ID field, so existing rows update instead of inserting again
Switching to insert and hoping the duplicates are few
Enabling duplicate rules and letting them block the second run
questions.explanation: Upsert matches incoming rows on the external ID, so a rerun updates the records that already landed and only inserts the rows that never made it, which is what makes an incremental load re runnable.

questions.question: An admin loads 200,000 Accounts with Data Loader. The org has an active duplicate rule on Account set to Alert. What happens to a row that matches an existing Account?
options: Nothing, because Data Loader is not a duplicate-aware path and the rule is bypassed
The rule is evaluated, no alert is shown during the load, and the matching row is not saved
The rule is evaluated and the load pauses so the admin can choose a surviving record for each match
Nothing, because duplicate rules apply only to records entered in the UI
questions.explanation: Salesforce overrides the duplicate rule setting for records added by the data import tools and by the APIs: no alert is shown, and a matching record cannot be saved. The rule is still evaluated, so an import is not a way around an active rule.

questions.question: A customer wants to stop duplicate Contacts at the point of entry but still allow an occasional legitimate near match to be saved with a warning. Which configuration meets both requirements?
options: A matching rule set to Block
A duplicate rule with a Block action and a narrow matching rule
A duplicate rule with an Allow and report action, paired with a matching rule tuned for fuzzy and blank handling
A validation rule on the Email field
questions.explanation: Allowing the save with a report gives the warning and the Duplicate Record Set work queue, while the matching rule must be tuned so the near matches are actually detected. Blocking would prevent the legitimate saves the customer wants to keep.

questions.question: A customer filters a large object constantly on a field that is not indexed, and also runs reports that read a small set of hot fields from the same object. Which two features address these?
options: A duplicate rule and a validation rule
Sharing rules and org wide defaults
A custom index on the filtered field and a skinny table for the hot fields
A scheduled dashboard and a report folder
questions.explanation: A custom index speeds the filtered queries, and a skinny table, which is a Support created copy of the most used fields, speeds the reads of the hot fields.

questions.question: Three downstream systems must react within seconds whenever an Opportunity stage changes, and the customer does not want each one polling Salesforce. Which design fits?
options: A nightly batch export that each system downloads
A synchronous REST call from Salesforce to each system on save
Change Data Capture or a Platform Event that publishes the change and lets the three systems subscribe
A shared spreadsheet refreshed hourly
questions.explanation: An event driven design publishes the change once and lets interested subscribers react in near real time, which is exactly what Change Data Capture and Platform Events are built for, while polling loads the org with needless requests.

questions.question: A migration package contains Opportunities, Accounts, Contacts, Products, and Opportunity Line Items. Which load order is correct?
options: Opportunities, then Accounts, then Contacts, then Products, then Line Items
Accounts, then Contacts, then Opportunities, then Products, then Opportunity Line Items
Contacts, then Accounts, then Products, then Line Items, then Opportunities
Line Items first, because they carry the most detail
questions.explanation: Parents must exist before the children that reference them, and Opportunity Line Items depend on Price Book Entries, which depend on Products and Price Books, so the parent to child order is the only one that resolves.

questions.question: During planning for a migration of 40,000 accounts, the consultant finds thousands of duplicate accounts and records with country values that do not match the target picklist. What should happen before the production load?
options: Load everything and clean up in Salesforce afterward
Load only the accounts that pass validation and leave the rest behind
Deduplicate and normalize the values in the source, then validate with a test load in a full sandbox
Import with the Data Import Wizard to force validation rules to fix the values
questions.explanation: Cleansing and deduplicating in the source is far cheaper than fixing records after they land in Salesforce, and a full sandbox test load proves the mapping and the counts first.

questions.question: An integration writes Opportunities every night and must bypass the new Amount validation rule, while sales users must not be able to. What is the correct approach?
options: Remove the validation rule and rely on training
Keep the validation rule and scope a bypass to the integration user through a custom permission or hierarchy setting the rule checks
Move Amount to required on the page layout
Have the integration write with the Data Import Wizard instead
questions.explanation: Validation rules are the layer that actually protects the object, so keep it and give the trusted integration a controlled bypass. Removing it or downgrading to a page layout requirement would leave the data unprotected.

questions.question: A sales operations lead reports that roughly 30 percent of open Opportunities have a blank Amount and a blank Close Date, and the forecast is unreliable. Which data quality dimension is failing, and what is the most direct first control?
options: Uniqueness, so enable duplicate rules on Opportunity
Completeness, so make Amount and Close Date required and enforce it with a validation rule
Validity, so convert Amount and Close Date to restricted picklists
Timeliness, so shorten the data stream refresh interval
questions.explanation: Blank values in required business fields are a completeness failure, and the direct control is making the fields required at the object level rather than only on the page layout. The other options name real dimensions but none of them fixes a missing value.

questions.question: An org enables a lead scoring model and finds that reps now contact almost only the segment they always contacted, while a previously unworked segment is never surfaced. What is the correct diagnosis?
options: The model needs a larger dataset
Einstein Activity Capture is broken
The model has learned the historical contact pattern and is reinforcing it, a bias and feedback loop problem, so the segment criteria and field set need review
The lead scores simply need refreshing more often
questions.explanation: The model reproduces the historical working pattern and the business follows it, which is a feedback loop created by biased training history, not a data volume or sync defect.

questions.question: A sales VP wants the system to tell reps which single action to take next on an at risk renewal, not just a probability. Which capability answers the requirement?
options: Einstein Lead Scoring
An Einstein Next Best Action strategy built in Flow on top of a prediction
Einstein Activity Capture
A validation rule on the Opportunity
questions.explanation: A recommendation is produced by a strategy layer that converts a prediction into an action, which is what Einstein Next Best Action does. A score or a sync feature does not produce advice.

questions.question: A sales org wants the agent to check order status in an external ERP and then draft a follow up email. What must the consultant configure?
options: Only a larger prompt template
Only a Data Cloud data stream
An action that reaches the ERP through a Flow or an Apex invocable method, attached to the relevant topic, plus a prompt template or action for the draft
A new permission set on the Opportunity object
questions.explanation: The agent can only run actions you attach, so reaching the ERP requires an action, and the drafting step is satisfied by a prompt template or another action. A data stream alone gives the agent nothing to run.

questions.question: A manager asks what unlocks coaching evidence from recorded sales calls, including talk ratio and competitor mentions.
options: Einstein Activity Capture
Opportunity Scoring factors
Einstein Conversation Insights, deployed alongside a recording consent process
A prompt template in Prompt Builder
questions.explanation: Conversation Insights records and transcribes calls and surfaces talk ratios and competitor mentions, and recording consent has to be handled wherever it is deployed.

questions.question: A regulator asks how the org ensures its lead scoring does not systematically exclude a customer group. Which principle is at stake and what is the control?
options: Transparency, so publish the model weights
Security, so encrypt the score field
Inclusivity, with outcome monitoring by segment and a named owner accountable for the result
Reliability, by refreshing scores more often
questions.explanation: Systematic exclusion is an inclusivity and accountability question, and the control is monitoring outcomes by segment with someone answerable for the finding.

questions.question: A field holding a customer's postal code is included in a scoring model and correlates strongly with a protected characteristic in that region. What should the consultant do?
options: Evaluate the field as a proxy, consider excluding it, and monitor outcome distribution by segment
Keep it because it improves accuracy
Encrypt the field
Move the field to a different object
questions.explanation: A strong proxy behaves like a protected attribute, so the control is to evaluate exclusion and then watch outcomes by segment. Encrypting or relocating the field leaves the correlation intact.

questions.question: Which statement about Einstein Lead Scoring data requirements is correct?
options: 200 converted leads in the last 24 months
At least 1,000 leads created in the last 200 days with at least 120 converted to an account and contact
1,000 converted leads in the last 12 months
No minimum, because the global model always applies
questions.explanation: Lead Scoring needs 1,000 leads created in the last 200 days and at least 120 converted, which is a different threshold set from Opportunity Scoring.

questions.question: A sales team wants a summary of an Opportunity written into a field on the record whenever the rep asks, with no conversation involved. Which tool fits?
options: An Agentforce agent with one topic per summary
Einstein Conversation Insights
A prompt template of the Record Summary type, grounded on the Opportunity and its related records
Einstein Opportunity Scoring
questions.explanation: A single grounded generation with known inputs is a prompt template job of the Record Summary type, not an agent or a scoring feature.
